data.narrative:
Caelux is a Series A–stage climate and energy company that has raised $75M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers, including well-funded entities such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, peer-median valuation analysis is not applicable here due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow peer set; only three or more datapoints would support a credible median approach in this case.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation tool. Using total capital raised ($75M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A–to–next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $150M. This represents the median point in the analysis.

The valuation analysis supports a range of $128M (low) to $172M (high), centered on $150M. This range reflects a ±15% sensitivity band around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer comparables at the same development stage and the reliance on a single methodological input. Additional clarity on burn rate, revenue traction, and capital requirements through the next funding round would refine this estimate.
